text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The cabinet decided Thursday to recommend to Parliament that parliamentary elections be held in May next year, and in April every four years in the future, cabinet spokesman Elemer Kiss announced.
- Hungary's seven parliamentary parties concurred Thursday on the need for a referendum on NATO accession in November.
- The head of the Central Registry and Election Office said his staff will need up to 50 days to prepare for a referendum, whose costs are estimated at 1.7 billion forints.
- NATO expects Hungary to carry out military reforms and enhance its defense potential said visiting U.S. Defense Secretary William Cohen.
- The Hungarian government views accession to both NATO and the European Union as of equal importance, said Industry and Trade Minister Szabolcs Fazakas.
- Hungary got the best marks in almost all areas covered by questionnaires sent back to the European Union last year, Vilaggazdasag has learned.

- Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin said his country sees no reason for changing its strategy regarding Romanian-Hungarian relations following Hungary's invitation to start NATO accession talks.
- A Hungarian consulate general in Romania is set to open in the building of the Calvinist Church in Cluj-Napoca on July 23.

- The Hungarian Energy Association (MET) is demanding that the privatization of the electricity sector be stopped, contracts be published and revised and a new privatization strategy based on the consensus of all parties involved be formulated.
- The radical reorganization of the nation's labor market is nearing completion, according to Labor Minister Peter Kiss.
- The inclemency of the weather caused damage 9 billion forints to the nation's agricultural sector this year.
- Industrial production prices went up 0.7 percent in May and were 19.1 percent higher than in the fifth month of 1996.
- The National Radio and Television Board (ORTT) gave a detailed explanation Thursday of its assessment of the winners in a recent tender for commercial television broadcasting rights.
- The CEO of MTM-SBS, one of two winners of the tender for national commercial television channels, is designing an image for its program incorporated under the name TV2.
- The privatization of K&H Bank (Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank) promises to be a success, according to State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.)
- The general meetings of Konzumbank and Corvinbank yesterday okayed the plan of their owner, the Hungarian Development Bank (MFB), to merge the two banks within three months.
- The post-tax profits of the General Banking & Trust Co. (AEB Rt.) were 1.28 billion forints in the first half of 1997.
- Magyar Suzuki Rt. sold 31,069 of its Swift models in the first half of the year, 29 percent more than in January-June 1996.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Experts who spoke on condition of anonymity said in Washington Thursday that only an American nuclear umbrella could defend Poland and the Czech Republic against a Russian invasion, while Hungary could not be saved even by such an umbrella.
